verdict.rationale: Notte documents cloud browser sessions as isolated instances you can control programmatically, and it markets its browsers as 'scalable'. That covers the programmatic session-management part of the story. Nothing in the pack documents concurrency limits or explicit fleet or parallel-session orchestration. missing for 10: documented concurrency limits per plan, explicit concurrent/fleet session management APIs (list/stop/monitor many sessions), independent or hands-on corroboration of parallel scale.

support.subject: As an automation-engineer, I can run a fleet of concurrent browser sessions with documented concurrency limits and programmatic session management

citations.quote: Sessions are isolated browser instances running in the cloud that you can control programmatically.
Fast, scalable browsers with anti-detection, proxies, and captcha solving.
Notte sessions expose a Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) endpoint that you can connect to with Playwright.
